Description:

Description:
The Overdue Amount can be filtered by a numeric From & To range, and its quick option is capped at the plan's total overdue.

Description: [New] Overdue Amount From and To set to the same value returns only plans whose overdue exactly equals it
Pre-requisite Data: Track1 = the plan-level tracking worklist; Plan1 = a plan whose overdue total is Ovd1; Plan2 = a plan whose overdue total is slightly below Ovd1; Plan3 = a plan whose overdue total is slightly above Ovd1.
Test Data: In the Overdue Amount filter enter From = Ovd1 and To = Ovd1 and apply.
Expected Output: The filter is inclusive at both ends, so the plan whose overdue equals the boundary value is returned while plans just below and just above it are excluded.
Verification Step: 1. Open Track1 and note the Overdue Amount of Plan1, Plan2 and Plan3. 2. Open the filter pane and enter Ovd1 in both the From and the To field. 3. Apply the filter. 4. Assert Plan1 is listed. 5. Assert Plan2 is not listed. 6. Assert Plan3 is not listed. 7. Clear the filter and assert all three plans return.

Description: [New] Overdue Amount filter with only the To value filled behaves as an upper limit
Pre-requisite Data: Track1 = the plan-level tracking worklist; Lim1 = an overdue value; Plan1 = a plan with overdue below Lim1; Plan2 = a plan with overdue exactly Lim1; Plan3 = a plan with overdue above Lim1.
Test Data: Leave the Overdue Amount From field blank, enter Lim1 in To and apply.
Expected Output: With From blank the filter treats the range as open at the bottom: every plan with an overdue amount up to and including Lim1 is returned, and plans above Lim1 are excluded. No validation error is raised for the blank From.
Verification Step: 1. Open Track1 and open the filter pane. 2. Leave Overdue Amount From empty and type Lim1 into To. 3. Apply and assert no validation error is shown for the blank From. 4. Assert Plan1 is listed. 5. Assert Plan2 is listed (the To boundary is inclusive). 6. Assert Plan3 is not listed. 7. Clear the To field and assert the unfiltered worklist returns.

Description: [New] Overdue Amount filter with only the From value filled behaves as a lower limit
Pre-requisite Data: Track1 = the plan-level tracking worklist; Lim1 = an overdue value; Plan1 = a plan with overdue below Lim1; Plan2 = a plan with overdue exactly Lim1; Plan3 = a plan with overdue above Lim1.
Test Data: Enter Lim1 in the Overdue Amount From field, leave To blank and apply.
Expected Output: With To blank the range is open at the top: every plan with an overdue amount of Lim1 or more is returned and plans below Lim1 are excluded, again with no validation error for the blank field.
Verification Step: 1. Open Track1 and open the filter pane. 2. Type Lim1 into Overdue Amount From and leave To empty. 3. Apply and assert no validation error is shown for the blank To. 4. Assert Plan2 is listed (the From boundary is inclusive). 5. Assert Plan3 is listed. 6. Assert Plan1 is not listed. 7. Clear the From field and assert the unfiltered worklist returns.

Description: [New] Overdue Amount From greater than To is rejected or returns an empty result without error
Pre-requisite Data: Track1 = the plan-level tracking worklist; Hi1 = a higher overdue value; Lo1 = a lower overdue value (Lo1 is less than Hi1).
Test Data: Enter From = Hi1 and To = Lo1 in the Overdue Amount filter and apply.
Expected Output: The screen handles the inverted range gracefully: either a clear validation message stops the search, or the grid simply returns no rows with an empty-state message. The application never crashes and never silently swaps the two values.

Assert either a validation message identifies the inverted range or the grid shows an empty result with a friendly message. 5. Assert no script error, spinner hang or blank screen occurs. 6. Assert the values entered are not silently swapped behind the scenes. 7. Correct the range to From = Lo1 and To = Hi1 and assert the expected plans are returned.

Description: [New] Plans with zero overdue are excluded by a positive From value and included when the range starts at zero
Pre-requisite Data: Track1 = the plan-level tracking worklist; Plan0 = a plan whose overdue amount is zero; Plan1 = a plan with a non-zero overdue amount; Val1 = a positive value at or below Plan1's overdue amount.
Test Data: Filter Overdue Amount From = Val1, then repeat with From = 0.
Expected Output: A positive lower bound filters out the zero-overdue plans, while a range starting at zero brings them back, so the column and the filter agree on what counts as zero overdue.
Verification Step: 1. Open Track1 and confirm Plan0 shows zero or blank in the Overdue Amount column. 2. Open the filter pane and set Overdue Amount From = Val1; apply. 3. Assert Plan1 is listed. 4. Assert Plan0 is not listed. 5. Change From to 0 and leave To blank; apply. 6. Assert Plan0 is now listed together with Plan1. 7. Confirm a blank Overdue Amount cell is treated the same way as an explicit zero.

Description: [New] The Overdue Amount filter accepts only numeric input and rejects text and negative values
Pre-requisite Data: Track1 = the plan-level tracking worklist; Txt1 = a non-numeric text string; Neg1 = a negative number; Val1 = a valid positive amount.
Test Data: Type Txt1 and then Neg1 into the Overdue Amount From/To fields, then enter Val1.
Expected Output: The From and To fields are strictly numeric: letters and symbols are not accepted, a negative value is rejected or blocked, and a valid amount is accepted and used for the search.
Verification Step: 1. Open Track1 and open the filter pane. 2. Type Txt1 into the Overdue Amount From field and assert the characters are not accepted. 3. Type Neg1 and assert the negative value is rejected or the minus sign is blocked. 4. Repeat steps 2-3 for the To field. 5. Enter Val1 in From and assert it is accepted. 6. Apply and assert the search runs and returns plans consistent with Val1. 7. Confirm decimal entry behaves per the currency format used by the other amount filters.

Description: [New] The Pay Now 'Overdue Amount' option is capped at the plan's total overdue and cannot be exceeded
Pre-requisite Data: Plan1 = a plan with a non-zero overdue total Ovd1; Over1 = any value greater than Ovd1; Track1 = the plan-level tracking worklist showing Plan1's Overdue Amount.
Test Data: Open Plan1 from Track1, choose Pay Now with the Overdue Amount option and try to enter Over1.
Expected Output: The Overdue Amount option defaults to Ovd1 (the same figure shown in the worklist column) and refuses any amount above it, so a user can never collect more than is actually overdue through this option.
Verification Step: 1. Open Track1 and note Plan1's Overdue Amount. 2. Open Plan1 and click Pay Now. 3. Select the Overdue Amount option. 4. Assert the amount defaults to Ovd1 and equals the worklist column value. 5. Try to enter Over1 and assert the entry is blocked or clamped back to Ovd1. 6. Assert an amount below Ovd1 is still permitted if partial payment is allowed, or is handled per the defined rule. 7. Confirm no payment can be submitted for more than Ovd1 through this option.

Description: [New] The Overdue Amount cap and column refresh after an overdue payment is collected
Pre-requisite Data: Plan1 = a plan with overdue total Ovd1; Track1 = the plan-level tracking worklist; Pay1 = a successful Pay Now payment for the full overdue amount of Plan1.
Test Data: Collect Pay1 against Plan1 using the Overdue Amount option, then return to Track1.
Expected Output: After the overdue amount is collected, the worklist Overdue Amount for the plan drops to zero and the Pay Now Overdue Amount option is capped at the new (zero) overdue, so the stale cap is never reused.
Verification Step: 1. Open Track1 and note Plan1's Overdue Amount Ovd1. 2. Open Plan1, use Pay Now with the Overdue Amount option and complete Pay1 for the full Ovd1. 3. Assert the affected installments move to the paid status. 4. Return to Track1 and refresh. 5. Assert Plan1's Overdue Amount now reads zero or blank. 6. Reopen Pay Now and assert the Overdue Amount option is now capped at zero or is unavailable. 7. Apply an Overdue Amount From filter above zero and assert Plan1 no longer appears.

Description: [New] The Overdue Amount column is included in the grid totals and in the export with matching figures

Add the visible Overdue Amount cells manually and assert the total matches. 4. Export Track1 and open Exp1. 5. Assert Exp1 contains the Overdue Amount column. 6. Assert each row's overdue value in Exp1 matches the on-screen value. 7. Assert the total in Exp1, if present, matches the on-screen total. 8. Change the filter and assert the total recalculates for the new visible set.
